messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] STREAMING_TAIL_LATENCY — streaming-proxy.p99 > 1.2s over 5m. Affected: EU region. PagerDuty: paged oncall (@oncall).

sandeep: on call, looking. initial check: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.8s, error spike for streaming chunk sends. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/streams/latency?from=now-10m :eyes:

maria: seeing a bunch of stalled SSE sockets on proxy2-eu-*. tcp retransmits + many connections in WRITE_PENDING. Also seeing a bump in 502/504 from proxy -> origin timeouts. stack traces in logs show repeated "proxy write timeout" followed by "client reset (EPIPE)".

aj: grep on proxy logs:
```
2026-03-15T18:12:02Z proxy2-eu-1 streaming: write timeout after 30000ms for conn id=0x1fae
2026-03-15T18:12:02Z proxy2-eu-1 streaming: write EPIPE when flushing chunk id=...
```

aj: also seeing per-connection queues grow. request sizes roughly normal but tail token emission is delayed. looks like outbound socket stalls + backpressure from client or kernel socket buffers.

taylor: hypothesis: proxy keepalive/write timeout + congestion on NIC + long-lived SSE clients that don't read quickly -> server side buffer backlog. When the write queue grows we hit proxy-level timeout and tear down connection which then shows up as p99 spikes.

leah: impacted customers flagged by support: payments-io (high traffic webhook stream), chat-widget-prod (low-latency chat). I've opened support threads and pinged account owners with our incident link. support-bot: posted templated customer note.

maria: quick check of infra: CPU/gpu not saturated. NIC tx drops on proxy2-eu-1: ifconfig shows tx dropped climbing in last 6m. kernel dmesg shows "skb: queue overrun" on that host.

aj: trying an immediate mitigation: 1) drain and restart proxy2-eu-1, 2) flip streaming route for eu -> prefer proxy pool A (fall back to websocket), 3) temporarily increase proxy write_timeout to 60s while we stabilize. I'm going to carry out (1) now.

oncall: handoff: oncall -> sandeep (primary), aj (secondary). tagged ops_sre for assistance.

devops-bot: deploy/ephemeral action: cordon proxy2-eu-1 and start replacement instance (ami: px-eu-20260310). logs will stream to #eng-infra.

aj: executed restart of proxy2-eu-1 (replaced). flipping route for eu to prefer pool-a now (traffic shift 25% -> 100% over 3min).

maria: after replacement + routing: p95 dropped to ~110ms, p99 ~240ms. still occasional stalls for long-lived connections > 60s (looks like a small subset of clients with very low read throughput).

sandeep: rolled write_timeout to 60s on all proxy2-eu instances as short-term mitigation (config change rolled, revision r2026-561). That reduces premature disconnects but we need root cause.

aj: ran a quick prometheus query to correlate:
```promql
sum(rate(streaming_proxy_write_time_bucket{region="eu"}[5m])) by (le)
```
shows heavy mass in buckets > 500ms during spike window. also:
```promql
sum(increase(node_network_transmit_errs_total{instance=~"proxy2-eu.*"}[10m]))
```
spiked on proxy2-eu-1.

maria: reproduction attempt: open several SSE clients that deliberately read slowly -> proxy queue grows then kernel tx drops appear on host. Looks like we hit kernel tx queue saturation (NIC-level) under certain client patterns.

leah: customer impact summary (so far): payments-io reported intermittent missing events for sessions lasting >30s. chat-widget-prod reported message lag for embedded widgets in EU; no message loss observed yet but visible latency spikes. CS notified customers at 18:30 UTC.

sandeep: action plan (short-term):
- keep write_timeout=60s for 2h
- replace sick proxy node(s) and continue shifting traffic to healthy pool
- enable websocket fallback for streaming when available (config toggle): streams.fallback.websocket=true
- add temporary rate/connection limit per-IP to protect proxies

aj: executed per-IP soft limit on long-lived SSE to 100 concurrent connections per IP via envoy-rate-limiter. should reduce resource hogging while we investigate.

maria: after soft-limit and node replacement p95 ~95ms p99 ~170ms. tail still occasionally hits ~800ms for >90s connections but overall backlog reduced.

support-bot: customers updated in threads: https://support.redwood/tickets/PR-4421, CH-998.

oncall: declaring this Sev2 and creating incident channel #incident/streaming-eu-tail-4201112222. Postmortem assigned to sandeep/maria/aj.

taylor: long-term items (post-incident):
- add per-connection telemetry for write queue length and kernel tx drops to alert earlier
- evaluate export of socket-level drops to metrics and set SLO for streaming tail p99 < 300ms
- improve fallback behavior to automatically shift long-lived slow-read clients to websocket or polling
- consider bypass path for high-throughput low-latency customers (dedicated proxies)

maria: saving logs and capture: /var/log/streaming/proxy2-eu-1/incident-4201112222.tar.gz. will attach to postmortem.

sandeep: next steps: I'll synthesize timeline and customer impact for postmortem (taking over incident channel). if anything else pops, ping me @sandeep, marking this thread for handoff in 30m. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Alert resolved: STREAMING_TAIL_LATENCY resolved at 2026-03-15T19:05:00Z (reduction in p99). Incident still active for post-incident analysis.

leah: final customer update posted at 19:10 UTC. closing support escalations once we finish RCA.

aj: quick note — logs indicate one container was hitting an older kernel driver with known skb bug; replacement AMI does not have that driver. include in RCA.

maria: adding tags for the incident: [streaming][sse][proxy][eu][p99][severe2]. saving thread.

support-bot: closing customer-facing thread for payments-io once we confirm no further retries needed.

sandeep: handoff summary for ops oncall: mitigations applied (node replacement, increased write_timeout, per-ip soft limits, websocket fallback toggle), current state: stable with residual tail anomalies limited to very long-lived slow clients. Postmortem owners: sandeep, maria, aj.

oncall: thanks all. moving to post-incident channel for writeup.
